PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

Welcome to the meeting of the Parks, Recreation & Community Services Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs and videotapes of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling
(818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

  MEETING AGENDA
  Monday, March 18, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

1.  ROLL CALL
  A. Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. The Agenda for the March 18, 2019, regular
  meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall on or before Friday, March 15, 2019.

2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes. The
  Commission may question the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. The Director may refer
  the matter to the proper section for investigation and report.
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before a motion is
  proposed.
  A.  Approval of the Minutes of the Commission special meeting held on January 28, 2019.
6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Community Center Drop-In Program Report
  B. Therapeutic Recreation Annual Report
  C. Section Activity Reports
  1.  Recreation & Community Services
  2.  Park Services

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  NEXT MEETING:
  April 15, 2019 – City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway
minutes_text:
PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION
  MEETING MINUTES
  Monday, March 18, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 2:32 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Babaian, Kalfayan, Michals, and President Pro Tem Wolfson
  Absent: President Asatryan

  A.  Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the March 18, 2019, regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall
  on or before Friday, March 15, 2019.

2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian read a list of upcoming City Council agenda
  items related to the Community Services & Parks Department (CSP).
3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  President Pro Tem Wolfson commented on the Arroyo Verdugo Greenway.

  Commissioner Michals commented on events that he attended: One Glendale Basketball
  Championship and the Cherry Blossom Festival, adding that the tea house was nicely renovated.

  Ms. Moreno Hernandez announced upcoming events organized or sponsored by the Community
  Services & Parks Department.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the Commission special meeting held on January 28, 2019.

  Moved:  Commissioner Michals
  Seconded: Commissioner Babaian

  That the minutes of the Commission special meeting held on January 28, 2019, be approved
  as submitted.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes:  Commissioners Babaian, Kalfayan, Michals, President Pro Tem Wolfson
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Asatryan
  Abstain:  None
  1
 6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Community Center Drop-In Program Report
  Sr. Community Services Supervisor Sevag Garabetian provided a PowerPoint presentation
  covering the following topics: four community centers, collaborations, drop-in programs, activity
  cards, gym at ARC, total drop-in participation, and fiscal impact.

  Commissioners asked how annual activity cards are promoted, how daily passes work, if the
  annual pass can be promoted more, and why Sparr Heights Community Center programs have
  fewer participants than the Adult Recreation Center if they both have the same amount of
  programs.

  B.  Therapeutic Recreation Annual Report
  Community Services Supervisor Kenneth Khan provided a PowerPoint presentation covering the
  following topics: program description, types of disabilities that participants may have, Club Maple
  Program special events and participation, and Get Fit Program description and participation.

  Commissioner Michals asked for the maximum number of participants we can have per program.

  C.  Section Activity Reports
  1.  Recreation & Community Services
  Mr. Garabetian provided a PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics: Parent’s
  Night Out, Table Tennis Tournament, holiday celebrations for seniors, presentations for
  seniors, Youth & Family Services, STAR Program, One Glendale After School Youth Sports
  Program, Trails & Open Space programs, and Go! Glendale Outdoors.

  2.  Park Services
  Deputy Director of Community Services & Parks Koko Panossian provided a brief overview of
  work orders completed by Park Services staff in the months of January and February and
  gave a PowerPoint presentation highlighting work completed at Brand Park – Doctor’s House,
  Lower Scholl Canyon Park, Riverwalk – South Partition, Adams Square Mini Park, Glorietta
  Park, City Hall, and Verdugo Park.

7.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 3:09 p.m.
